item.text: {"search_note":"I found no credible 2023 evidence that Putin actively protected political equality for minorities, women, excluded groups, opposition regions, or unpopular viewpoints. The best counterevidence is only formal legal participation, not substantive equal treatment.","evidence":[{"title":"Russia: 2023 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices","publisher":"U.S. Department of State","date":"22 Apr 2024","url":"https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia","summary":"The report says no laws formally limited participation of women and minority groups, and they did participate. But it also says women were only about 18% of elected seats, ethnic Russians dominated the political and administrative system, and authorities restricted political participation and organized sham elections in occupied Ukrainian territories. This is weak formal counterevidence only.","question_ids":["4B.7","4B.2","4B.3"]},{"title":"Russia: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2023","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2023","summary":"Freedom House says women are underrepresented in politics, national minority regions are tightly controlled, some republics do not have direct gubernatorial elections, and LGBT+ people face major barriers. It also says the state targeted minority groups and kept politics dominated by ethnic Russians.","question_ids":["4B.7","4B.4","4B.5"]},{"title":"Russia: Nations in Transit 2023 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2023","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2023","summary":"Freedom House says Russia’s political leadership and ruling coalition embraced an isolationist, militant vision, local autonomy was curbed, and ethnic minority regions were more visible targets of discrimination and central control during the war.
